title: The Art of Public Speaking
author: J. Berg Esenwein & Dale Carnegie
blurb: Dale Carnegie's first book, written before How to Win Friends: beating stage fright, killing monotony, and speaking so people listen.

monotony.e: The monotony of the long drive made him sleepy.

self-confidence.e: Practice gave her the self-confidence to sing on stage.

audience.e: The audience laughed at the first joke.

cards.title: Everyone gets stage fright
cards.text: The book opens with the question every beginner asks: how do I stop being afraid in front of people? The authors promise it can be learned.
cards.quote: the fear that paralyzes me before an audience
cards.qMean: The fear that freezes you when everyone is watching.
cards.qLife: Your mind going blank during a class presentation.
cards.cap: Robert Dighton, The Specious Orator · public domain

cards.title: Be like the calm horses
cards.text: From a train window you see some horses bolt at the noise and others keep grazing, used to it. Speakers grow calm the same way — by facing audiences again and again.
cards.quote: some horses feed near the track and never even pause to look up at the thundering cars
cards.qMean: Repeated exposure makes frightening things ordinary.
cards.qLife: After ten presentations, the eleventh barely scares you.
cards.cap: Franz Marc, Grazing Horses, 1911 · public domain

cards.title: Confidence needs content
cards.text: You can't fake confidence. Know your subject so well that you have something real to be confident about.
cards.quote: to acquire self-confidence you must have something in which to be confident.
cards.qMean: Real confidence comes from being well prepared.
cards.qLife: Knowing your project inside out before the client meeting.
cards.cap: Reading room, Bibliothèque Mazarine, 19th c. · public domain

cards.title: Don't drone
cards.text: The deadliest fault in speaking is monotony — the same tone, pace and pitch. Vary them and people stay awake.
cards.qMean: Speaking in one flat tone ruins a talk.
cards.qLife: A lecturer who reads slides in the same voice for an hour.
cards.cap: William Hogarth, The Sleeping Congregation · public domain

cards.title: Be natural — by practice
cards.text: Telling someone to 'be natural' doesn't help. Natural speaking is built by copying what good speakers do until it becomes your own.
cards.quote: It is useless to warn the student that he must be natural.
cards.qMean: Just saying 'be natural' doesn't make anyone natural.
cards.qLife: Rehearsing a toast many times so it sounds effortless.
